Text.p251c7ab9f721:
Rougarou
These massive, undead wolves are the favored 
servants of Titania, the Autumn Queen of the Fae. 
They were some of the few members of her court 
that were deemed dangerous enough to be doomed 
to imprisonment in Nythera alongside her, but now 
that she is free, so are they.
Despite their bestial forms, Rougarou are keenly 
intelligent and dangerously cunning. The Queen 
uses them to hunt down those who have displeased 
her, employing them as her assassins and enforcers, 
but when not serving her, they roam the Knotwoods, 
walking the old paths and hunting Neverborn and 
human alike.
For a Rougarou, this hunting is merely entertainment; 
their rotting bodies require no physical sustenance, 
and often, the raw meat they devour rots in their 
gut or slips out between the bones of their skeletal 
ribcage. The memory of hunger, however, is sated 
by their feeding, and for most Rougarou, that is 
more than enough reason to kill.
When needed, Rougarou can stand and walk on their 
hind legs, which has reignited superstitions about 
werewolves among those who have glimpsed them 
doing this. Unlike a werewolf, however, 
a Rougarou remains dangerous no 
matter the phase of the moon, 
and silver has no more effect 
upon them than it would 
a human.

Text.p6d4c941caec3:
Bayou Gremlin
The Bayou is filled with many creatures, and there's 
certainly an argument to be made that the Bayou 
Gremlin is the most intelligent of them all. Originally 
little more than savages living in small packs in the 
depths of the swamp, the Gremlins came into their 
own when humans arrived in Malifaux.
Gremlins raise their young through mimicry. 
Despite the average Gremlin litter consisting of 
around ten to twenty baby Gremlins, a Gremlin 
mother can only breastfeed two children at a time. 
Females or particularly attractive children are given 
priority when it comes to selecting which Gremlins 
will receive this attention. The rest of the litter are 
ignored and forced to follow the adults around, 
trying to figure out how life works by copying them 
and hoping that it works out.
This mimicry served the Gremlins well when 
they decided to start learning from humans. They 
learned about clothing (the most important people 
always have the biggest hat), how to shoot firearms 
(so much damage!), how to construct crude walls 
(and, eventually, houses), how to domesticate 
the Bayou pigs (which had been their primary 
predators), and, most importantly in their minds, 
how to brew moonshine.
With these "borrowed" advancements, the Gremlin 
population swiftly boomed out of control. The 
Guild has recently realized that Gremlins could be a 
serious threat to their dominance of Malifaux... and 
it's only a matter of time before the Gremlins realize 
that, too.

Text.pacd5603155a3:
Bayou Boss
Given enough food, a Gremlin will never really 
stop growing. Thus, some of the most prolific and 
successful Gremlins are also some of the largest of 
their kind, which comes in handy when intimidating 
smaller Gremlins into handing over their food. For a 
long time, it was rare to see any Gremlins larger than 
a human child, simply because they were the primary 
targets of hungry pigs looking for a good meal.
Since the arrival of humans and the sweeping 
changes that human knowledge brought to Gremlin 
society, these larger Gremlins have become more 
common. More often than not, these Bayou Bosses 
use their increased size, strength, and (sometimes) 
intelligence to bully, cajole, and extort their smaller 
kin into subservience. 
The smaller Gremlins, for their part, are more or 
less comfortable with this situation. It's a lesson that's 
beaten into them as children the first time a young 
Gremlin tries to order an adult around, and those 
that don't learn that lesson by adulthood tend to end 
up getting tossed into the pig pen to shut them up. In 
a way, Gremlin society revolves around the various 
Bayou Bosses of the swamp. They determine when 
a Gremlin village will work with humans, what sort 
of food the village should cook, and when it's time 
to start (or end) a feud with one of their neighbors.

Text.pf116714e1738:
Slop Hauler
There are few things in life that pigs like more than 
eating. One of those things is eating without having 
to work for their food, which makes Slop Haulers 
some of their favorite Gremlins. Unfortunately, 
it's not uncommon for the chef to become the 
main course in the midst of all the feeding hogs, so 
experienced Slop Haulers tend to be rather quick 
on their feet.
Despite the risks involved with feeding a village's 
pigs, there are some significant perks to the job. 
Most importantly, perhaps, is that Slop Haulers get 
first pick of the food being given to the pigs, some 
of which is better than the food given to the village's 
Gremlins. Eating too much, however, might result in 
the Slop Hauler growing slow and fat, which results 
in the unfortunate Gremlin looking even more 
appetizing to the pigs they feed.
In addition to the threats of pigs and overeating, 
Slop Haulers also have to keep an eye on their 
fellow Gremlins. The position of Slop Hauler is 
highly coveted among Gremlins, due to the food 
perks, and more than one veteran Slop Hauler has 
had their career ended by having a bucket of slop 
thrown onto them while they were in the middle of 
feeding a particularly hungry pig.
The effectiveness of this tactic has been noted by 
the Slop Haulers who used it to get their position. 
When pressed into battle, Slop Haulers will often 
throw the vilest, most disgusting slop they can find at 
their enemies, grossing their opponents out even as

Text.p5f21f04b3ad9:
Moon Shinobi
The Gremlins that serve the master craftsman known 
only as the Brewmaster are a special lot. In order 
to join the enigmatic order of the Moon Shinobi, a 
Gremlin has to renounce all ties to their family and 
swear an oath of loyalty to the Brewmaster alone. In 
return for this, the Gremlin is given all the alcohol 
that they can drink... and then a bit more. Those 
who survive the initiation process (and many do not) 
are then deemed to be in an appropriate state of 
inebriation to learn the secrets of Drunken Gremlin 
Kung Fu.
The Gremlins are kept drunk (and, arguably, 
poisoned) throughout the entire training process, 
ensuring that they have the proper mindset to 
grasp the secrets taught to them by the Brewmaster. 
Even after a Gremlin has mastered their training 
and become a full-fledged Moon Shinobi, they are 
given ready access to as much alcohol as they wish, 
ensuring the sobriety is nothing more than a distant, 
unpleasant memory.
Though he draws upon other servants from time 
to time, the Moon Shinobi are the only ones that 
the Brewmaster trusts with his sensitive secrets. For 
the most part, the Moon Shinobi are too drunk to 
remember or even care about their lord's secrets, but 
even if one of them were to sober up, their loyalty to 
the Brewmaster is unshakable. 
It is rumored that the Moon Shinobi - or even the 
Brewmaster - might be pawns of the Ten Thunders, 
but that's just too complicated of a thought for most 
Moon Shinobi to process. They just do whatever the 
Brewmaster asks of them, and in return, he ensures 
that their flasks are never 
empty.

Text.p8d0c8220a6eb:
Piglet
Gremlins have an uneasy relationship with Piglets. 
It's common knowledge among most Gremlins that 
baby pigs grow up to be adult pigs, so that instills 
a healthy amount of caution into most Gremlins 
when they interact with Piglets. On the other hand, 
Piglets are easier to train than adult pigs, and it's not 
uncommon for a Gremlin to take a shine to a certain 
Piglet and decide to raise it as a pet.
In a way, these relationships mirror the relationship 
that a human has with a particularly violent pet 
dog. The animal is useful for self-defense or guard 
duty, and it can certainly provide a degree of 
companionship, but it's not the sort of thing that a 
rational person would let run around unsupervised. 
Gremlins, however, tend to be somewhat irrational 
creatures, and as a result, it's not unusual to hear 
stories about a young Gremlin getting cornered and 
devoured by someone's pet piglet. The common 
response to these situations is to hit the offending 
Piglet over the top of the head with a thick stick while 
shouting "Bad Pig!" at the animal, which is believed 
to make the pig regret its choice of meals.
Piglets tend to grow up a bit faster than their Earth 
counterparts, so it's not uncommon for a Gremlin 
village to butcher its pigs while they're still young. 
Part of this is a matter of ease, as it's easier for a 
small Gremlin to string up and butcher a Piglet than 
it is to do the same to a full-grown pig.
In the wild, Piglets tend to accompany their mother 
on her meandering Bayou journeys, relying upon 
her for much of their defense. When the situation 
calls for it, however, a Piglet is more than capable 
of charging into combat and making a nuisance of 
itself, as the squirming, energetic creatures tend to 
be quite distracting when their opponent is trying to 
focus on a greater threat.

Text.pa28bd131c60b:
Bayou Gator
Bayou Gators are one of the most efficient ambush 
predators in the swamps of Malifaux. They frequently 
wait in or near the water, holding still and hoping 
to be mistaken for a harmless, floating log. When 
their prey approaches the water for a drink, the gator 
leaps out at blinding speed, snaps its jaws around 
whatever limb it can catch, and attempts to drag its 
prey back into the water to drown it. 
Once in the water, Bayou Gators begin twisting their 
bodies in the infamous "death roll," a maneuver that 
uses torque to disorient and dismember prey much 
larger than itself. The thrashing (and screaming, in 
the case of humans or Gremlins) of those who have 
been unfortunate enough to be caught by one of 
these large predators has given them a reputation as 
violent murderers in Gremlin villages... which really 
isn't too far off the mark, all things considered.
Hungry Bayou Gators have been known to charge 
after a potential meal for staggering distances, 
sometimes even climbing up trees to catch hiding 
(and often very surprised) prey. Worse yet, the 
Bayou Gators will sometimes remain in the trees, 
uncertain how to get down, until potential prey 
passes underneath it. 
These "Drop Gators" are relatively rare in the Bayou, 
but all it takes is a single encounter with such a 
creature to make a traveler wary of creaky branches 
for the rest of her days.

Text.pf61ccd577d6e:
Bayou Chicken
The chickens of the Bayou were brought to Malifaux 
over a hundred years ago, during the days of the 
first Breach. It's unknown exactly how they entered 
the swamp, but it's likely that a flock of the birds 
escaped from a local farmer or rancher and settled 
down in the swamp to live out the rest of their lives 
in freedom. 
Over the next hundred years, the latent magic of 
Malifaux seeped into the bodies of each successive 
generation of chickens, eventually growing them 
to their current six-foot-tall height. The Bayou 
Chickens were prolific, and they spread quickly 
across the swamp, taking roost in the drier portions 
of the muck and slime. 
Unfortunately, the rapid expansion of the Bayou 
Chickens was cut off almost as quickly as it began. At 
roughly the same time, the Gremlins and pigs of the 
swamp started to take notice of the strange new birds 
in their home and just how delicious their eggs were. 
Soon the Bayou Chickens were having to defend 
their nests from constant raids from Gremlin and 
pig alike, and the constant stress resulted in only the 
most high-strung and paranoid chickens surviving 
to raise their young. The trait started breeding true, 
and now all the Bayou Chickens in the swamp are 
prone to nervousness and hypertension.

Text.p78e1846a230a:
Union Thug
The Miners and Steamfitters Union employs some 
of the greatest minds of the current generation... 
as well as a large number of uneducated miners, 
many of whom came to Malifaux as convicts who 
have since had their prison contacts purchased 
and destroyed by the Union. As a result, there 
are always plenty of people willing to rough up or 
intimidate the Union's enemies. 
Whether intimidating Guild Reporters into 
forgetting a troublesome story or shaking down a 
fellow Union member for his late dues, these thugs 
are the strong, unsubtle arm of the Union. They 
don't ask many questions, and in return, the Union 
takes care of them, providing them with good pay 
and, in the event that they're arrested by the Guild, 
a better lawyer than they could ever afford on their 
own. For most of these rough men and women, it's 
more than anyone else has ever given them, and 
for that, the Union has earned their loyalty.

Text.p7e54c92f3a3d:
Steamborg 
Executioner
The first Steamborg Executioners were the creations 
of the ancient inhabitants of Malifaux. The remains 
of these amalgamations of flesh and steel were 
unearthed by M&SU miners in the early days of the 
organization's formation, and Viktor Ramos' study 
of the flesh-grafting techniques used on the (longdead) creatures was one of the primary factors in 
the creation of pneumatic limbs for injured humans.
It wasn't until years later that Howard Langston 
was injured while Ramos was visiting a work site. 
Realizing that the injured miner was the perfect 
candidate for experimentation - his body was far 
too damaged to be saved by traditional pneumatics - 
Ramos whisked Langston to his lab and transformed 
him into the first modern Steamborg Executioner.
Since then, the number of Steamborg Executioners 
has been slowly but steadily increasing among the 
ranks of the M&SU. Nearly all are injured miners 
whose lives have been saved by Ramos and his best 
Steamfitters, which has given them a near-fanatic 
devotion to the Union and its president. The Guild's 
Amalgamation Office has attempted to confiscate 
and destroy the Steamborg Executioners multiple 
times, citing the illegal use of amalgamation 
in their construction, but thus far, public 
opinion has sided firmly 
with "those poor 
injured miners."

Text.pba5b90a878e9:
Gunsmith
The name "Gunsmith" is the codename given to 
the troubleshooters of the Miners and Steamfitters 
Union. When a Union boss is having problems that 
a group of thugs or political pressure can't solve, they 
instruct their subordinates to "see a Gunsmith about 
my pistol." 
The name is a reference to the wide variety of heavily 
modified pistols which the Gunsmiths carry, as well 
as to their specialized ammunition. These weapons 
ensure that a Gunsmith is able to bring the maximum 
amount of force to bear in any given situation.
Gunsmiths operate independent of most oversight 
and are trusted to accomplish their assigned tasks 
with speed and efficiency. They rely first on their 
reputations to diffuse situations, which often works, 
even when dealing with the Guild. Even the rumor of 
a Gunsmith's presence is sometimes enough to force 
the Union's enemies to concede to their demands.
Most Gunsmiths prefer peaceful solutions like this, 
as it keeps the Arcanist influence over the Union 
out of sight and mind. When pressed, however, a 
Gunsmith can be a fearsome opponent, and those 
who survive a battle against one rarely wish to repeat 
the experience.

Text.p29583aedaefa:
Showgirl
The women who make up the stage show at the Star 
Theater are some of the most famous, and desired, in 
all Malifaux. All of them are charming and beautiful, 
able to turn heads wherever they walk, and their 
careers as burlesque dancers have replaced what 
little modesty they might have had upon arriving in 
the city with boldness and confidence.
Due to their employer's Arcanist ties, each of the 
Showgirls employed by the Star Theater is also 
trained as an Arcanist agent. They assist her in 
smuggling Soulstones through the sewers beneath 
the theater, provide a distraction for other Arcanist 
operatives, and serve as liaisons between various 
Arcanist cells both in Malifaux City and beyond 
its walls.
In exchange for their services, the Showgirls are 
frequently taught snippets of magical lore, which, 
unbeknownst to most of the other Arcanists, are then 
shared freely among the rest of the Star's employees. 
While it's not uncommon to find a Showgirl who 
has mastered the art of summoning fire or lightning 
to her defense, most tend to favor 
illusions and other more subtle 
magics that can help both their 
life on the stage and their life 
in the shadows.

Text.p785e6207d72f:
Steamfitter
These spellcasters are ostensibly employed by the 
Union in order to keep its various mining constructs 
enchanted and functional. In reality, however, they 
are the core of the Arcanist movement, the men and 
women who believe that the use of magic should be 
free to everyone with the talent for it.
Steamfitters are technically regulated by the Guild, 
but after a decade of fighting with the Union over 
the specifics of that regulation, not to mention the 
greater threat posed by the Arcanists, the Guild has 
more or less left the licensing and regulation of the 
Steamfitters to the Union. Even the Witch Hunters 
are a bit unclear about just what a Steamfitter is 
capable of doing, but thus far, there just hasn't been 
time to investigate them in any great depth.
With access to the hidden vaults of the Arcanists, 
there is almost no bit of magical knowledge that a 
Steamfitter cannot access, given enough time and 
urgency. Most of them are quite adept spellcasters, 
and their profession all but demands that they 
be familiar with constructs and other forms of 
machinery.

Text.p00636e6acc81:
Oxfordian Mage
The Oxford University of Metaphysical Studies 
occupies a strange gray area in the eyes of the 
Guild. While Oxford's teachings are contrary to 
the Thalarian Doctrine, political pressure from the 
United States resulted in the Guild agreeing not to 
prosecute the University or its graduates for their 
arcane practices.
For the most part, this was an acceptable enough 
compromise, for the rituals and incantations taught 
by the Oxfordian professors were seen as outdated 
and cumbersome by the Guild. It was only after 
the first Oxfordian graduates traveled to Malifaux 
and learned that their spells were significantly more 
powerful than they had been on Earth that the Guild 
realized they may have made a terrible mistake.
Today, the travel of Oxfordian graduates to Malifaux 
is heavily restricted by the Guild. At great expense and 
risk, the Arcanists have smuggled many Oxfordian 
Mages into Malifaux to bolster their numbers. They 
have proven to be a devastating weapon against the 
organization's enemies, particularly when they work 
together to bolster each other's arcane rituals.
In order to protect their identities (and the safety 
of their alma mater), most of these mages wear 
masks while on assignment, 
thus preventing the Guild 
from comparing any of 
their likenesses to the 
pictures found in 
old Oxfordian 
yearbooks.

Text.p5773fdf37278:
Soulstone Driller
These worm-like constructs are among the newest 
of the mining constructs to roll out of the design 
workshops of Viktor Ramos. Unlike the Rock 
Hopper, which just digs for Soulstones like a human 
miner (albeit with far fewer complaints or accidents), 
the Soulstone Driller is actually capable of sensing 
the valuable gemstones in the ground and then 
burrowing directly to them.
Unfortunately, the worm-like design of the Soulstone 
Driller leaves it unable to excavate Soulstones itself, 
so it is frequently paired up with human miners who 
are tasked with entering the tunnels behind it to 
excavate the revealed gems. 
Because the tunnels created by a Soulstone Driller 
tend to be cramped and more than a little bit 
dangerous, the construct is frequently set with 
multiple Soulstones along its drill-like head, enabling 
it to absorb the souls of its crew, should they be 
killed in a tunnel collapse or cave-in. This has led to 
many miners refusing to work alongside Soulstone 
Drillers for fear of having their soul trapped after 
death, but the Union has taken steps to mitigate this 
fear by offering higher wages to those willing to work 
alongside a Soulstone Driller.
Though they were designed for mining, Ramos made 
certain that Soulstone Drillers were also capable of 
holding their own in combat. When employed in this 
way, the constructs dig their way through the ground, 
hunting the enemy from below before bursting up 
from the ground beneath them.
The Arcanists frequently remove the Soulstones 
from a Driller that is intended for combat purposes, 
but sometimes, they leave them attached in the hope 
that the Driller's rampage will result in a cache of 
fully charged Soulstones for no further effort on 
their part.

Text.pc91a3f4d4a16:
Rock Hopper
Rock Hoppers are the name given to the most 
common of the M&SU's various mining constructs. 
While not particularly beloved by the miners who 
work alongside them (they have a tendency to be a bit 
clumsy and have accidentally stepped on more than 
one miner's foot, shattering bones and often leading 
to an expensive pneumatic replacement), they are 
reliable and require little maintenance. That has 
been enough to keep them in service despite their 
many "quirks."
While it is capable of wielding a mining pick with 
the same skill as a human, it is the pneumatic drill 
on a Rock Hopper's arm that makes it invaluable 
to the Union. Rather than having to risk lives and 
the potential of a collapsed tunnel with dynamite, 
a Rock Hopper can quickly bore its way through 
hard stone, which helps to keep accidents (and thus, 
injured worker payouts) to a minimum.
Though slow and somewhat cumbersome, Rock 
Hoppers have been pressed into combat by 
Steamfitters on more than one occasion. Their 
pneumatic drills make them incredibly dangerous to 
others, and since they were designed to drill through 
solid stone, they remain effective against the Guild's 
ever-increasing suite of armored battle constructs.
In order to cover their tracks, the Union has allowed 
a number of Rock Hoppers to be sold into the 
private sector, ensuring that they can always claim 
that any Rock Hoppers who show up in battle 
against the Guild cannot be directly linked back to 
them. Indeed, the Union sometimes even abandons 
a Rock Hopper after a mission, ensuring that it falls 
into the hands of a would-be artificer with no ties to 
either the Union or the Arcanists.

Text.p948fb29ec5e7:
Large Arachnid
Unlike other Arcanist constructs, many of which are 
repurposed machines that were originally designed 
to mine Soulstones, the Large Arachnids were 
purposefully built for combat. Based on the Steam 
Arachnids that were originally designed to search 
cramped tunnels for Soulstone veins, the Large 
Arachnids are the Arcanist response to the Guild's 
increasing reliance upon constructs. 
Armed with industrial saw blades and programmed to 
dismantle their targets, Large Arachnids are capable 
of dismantling other constructs with alarming speed. 
They can then use the pieces of the fallen construct 
to patch up any damage they suffer in the battle, an 
interesting quirk of the prototypes that was enhanced 
with later models.
The biggest advantage of the Large Arachnid is the 
amount of resources required to build them. Coming 
in at half the price of one of the Guild's Peacekeeper 
constructs, Large Arachnids are downright affordable 
in comparison. More importantly, to the Arcanists 
at least, they're also half the size of a Peacekeeper, 
which makes it easier to hide them in work sheds 
and back rooms when they are not in use.

Text.p97a2e488bf1c:
Arcanist Smuggler
Though the Arcanists preach a philosophy of 
unregulated magic use for the common man, 
philosophy doesn't go very far when it comes time 
to pay the bills. To fund their shadowy war with 
the Guild, the Arcanists have resorted to smuggling 
Soulstones back to Earth, where they can sell each 
stone for a fraction of the Guild's inflated prices and 
still walk away with a small fortune. These stones 
are unregulated, allowing nations to amass magical 
power without the Guild's knowledge.
Getting a Soulstone through the Breach is a difficult 
process, and no Arcanist Smuggler worth her salt 
relies too heavily on any one method, lest the Guild 
catch on to what she is doing. Swallowing Soulstones 
is one way to get the valuable stones through Guild 
checkpoints, but the unpleasant retrieval method 
and physical limit on how many of the Soulstones 
can be moved at any one time make this impractical 
for large shipments.
Most Smugglers rely upon hiding Soulstones in 
secret compartments in their luggage or clothing, 
which allows them to bring the valuable stones 
back to Earth by the score. Some of them bribe 
the guardsmen working at the train stations to look 
the other way, while others draw upon their innate 
magic to hide the Soulstones in more esoteric ways, 
such as shifting them just out of phase with reality or 
teleporting them from one suitcase to another as the 
guardsmen check their bags.
Whatever their method, Arcanist 
Smugglers live a dangerous life, 
and it tends to make them 
paranoid. Being caught in 
the possession of stolen 
Soulstones is a death 
sentence, and all it 
takes is a single 
mistake to end a 
Smuggler's life.

Text.pcfaf6740c655:
December Cultist
The members of the Cult of December pay homage 
to an ancient entity of hunger and frost. December's 
whisper is subtle, heard in desperate times of famine 
and despair, and it draws the desperate and hungry 
to the distant Ten Peaks. In those frozen mountains, 
December's newest cultist is welcomed into her new 
life by his other servants, who teach her how to 
survive in her harsh new home.
Survival in the Ten Peaks, as it turns out, often 
involves cannibalism, and those who cannot make 
peace with hunting and feeding upon the lowlanders 
below are eventually devoured by those cultists with 
less discerning appetites. Those who prove willing 
to embrace the harsh lifestyle of the cult and swear 
fealty to the Tyrant known as December are trained

Text.pb4f47d3c20d8:
Thunder Archer
The Three Kingdoms heavily restricts the ownership 
and possession of firearms, which has made the bow 
the weapon of choice for outlaws and drifters. It is 
from these lawless ranks that the Thunder Archers 
recruit their students, drawing them into a tight-knit 
family of specialists who work together to teach 
the students not just how to become better archers 
but how to respect authority and live by a code of 
conduct far older than themselves.
The Thunder Archers hide their faces behind a wide 
metal helmet engraved with the symbol of an eye. 
Legend has it that the eye was once the insignia of 
an elite unit of archers fielded by the bloody general 
Izamu. The Archers of the Silent Eye were among 
the first of his army to rebel, ending his life in a hail 
of arrows... but not before the general butchered 
half of the unit. 
Today, the Thunder Archers serve the Ten 
Thunders. The eye on their helmets is seen as a 
symbol of good luck, for those who see the eye and 
survive have the favor of the Ten Thunders... and 
those who do not are found dead 
in the streets with a single 
arrow shot through 
their heart.

Text.p7ecb8cd27e07:
Rail Worker
Working on the rails is one of the most dangerous 
jobs in Malifaux. Between the frantic pace expected 
by most overseers, the dangerous pneumatic 
machines used for driving rivets, and the lumbering 
constructs that carry heavy piles of steel rails up 
and down the track, there are plenty of ways that a 
worker can lose their limbs or lives.
Before Mei Feng arrived, an injured worker had 
little option other than to place themselves in debt 
to the Guild or Union so deeply that there was rarely 
a chance they could repay it. When Mei Feng took 
over the supervision of the Foundry, the M&SU 
division responsible for the steady expansion of 
Malifaux's growing railway network, she earned the 
loyalty of its workers by tending to their medical 
needs without any expectation of repayment.
In return, the rail workers have pledged their loyalty 
to Mei Feng, fighting alongside her for the Union, 
the Arcanists, the Ten Thunders, or whichever 
other faction she happens to support today. The 
simple, stoic demeanors of these men and women 
hide cunning minds that are honed by their constant 
attempts to figure out just 
which side they're fighting 
on... and to whom their 
rail boss ultimately 
owes her loyalty.

Text.p1b05dcdcbba8:
Ten Thunder Brother
Life in the Three Kingdoms is difficult for those who 
are born without rank. It is even more difficult for 
those who have ambition and wish for more than the 
life of a farmer or servant can offer. Many of these 
disenfranchised men and women turn to criminal 
organizations to obtain the money and power their 
birth denied them.
The term "Ten Thunder Brother" is an inaccurate 
translation for "Shí léi jiazú," which means something 
closer to "Ten Thunder family" in its native Mandarin. 
Still, the name has spread through the years, to the 
point where even female members are referred to as 
"brothers" by their fellow thugs. 
The Ten Thunder Brothers hide their identities 
behind steel mempo and masks which depict the 
faces of leering oni. Anonymity is one of a Brother's 
most dangerous weapons, and it has created a culture 
of fear surrounding not just the Brothers but also the 
Ten Thunders. Generally, those who would speak 
out against the organization's money laundering, 
protection rackets, and smuggling rings are unable 
to give accurate descriptions of the Brothers to the 
authorities... any of 
whom might even be 
one of the masked 
thugs themselves.

Samurai
Within the Three Kingdoms, only the most 
powerful and high-ranking nobles are allowed to 
own and carry firearms. When the nobles hailing 
from Japan go to battle, they do so armed with the 
best weapons and armor that their vast fortunes 
can purchase. Most often this takes the form of a 
shoulder-mounted Gatling cannon and an advanced 
suit of powered armor modeled after the armor of 
their samurai ancestors.
These modern samurai tend not to stray far from 
Japan and their holdings there, but a small handful 
of them have traveled to Malifaux at the behest of 
the Ten Thunders, either as willing partners of the 
crime syndicate or as the unfortunate victims of 
extortion or blackmail.
Regardless of their reasons for serving the Ten 
Thunders, these Samurai are dangerous warriors who 
are more than capable of destroying their enemies 
at range or in close combat. More importantly, 
however, they are natural leaders with deep pockets, 
and anyone who runs afoul of a Samurai will find 
themselves harried relentlessly 
until either they or the Samurai 
is dead.

Text.pd8a4babc3a91:
Torakage
For years, families within the Three Kingdoms 
practiced a form of warfare that was firmly dictated 
by rules and honor. The Torakage were a group 
of highly skilled men and women whose covert 
methods of assassination and espionage went against 
everything the Three Kingdoms believed. Though 
their dishonorable actions were publicly decried 
by the noble houses, all of them eventually turned 
to the Torakage to remove troublesome rivals or 
ambitious underlings.
Although the Torakage have slipped into legend 
in the Three Kingdoms, the Katanaka Clan - and 
thus, the Ten Thunders - have continued to employ 
the Torakage well into modern times. They are a 
scalpel that the Ten Thunders wield with restraint, 
lest their existence and techniques become common 
knowledge. The Oyabun does not want to contend 
with other crime families resurrecting the ancient 
practice of employing the Torakage.
In Malifaux, the Torakage operate more openly, 
as the Oyabun is confident that few, if any, of its 
residents have ever heard of the Torakage lessons or 
lived to tell others of their encounter with the silent, 
masked assassins.

Oiran
Though they are frequently dismissed by those 
outside the Ten Thunders as simple entertainers and 
prostitutes, within the ranks of the crime syndicate, 
the Oiran are treated with respect and deference.
Oiran are skilled information gatherers who disguise 
their rigorous training and ruthless natures beneath 
downturned eyes and humble demeanors, playing 
the part of a subservient mistress or humble servant 
in order to better eavesdrop on the conversations 
of their employers and bed-fellows. They are the 
thumb that the Ten Thunders has placed upon the 
pulse of Malifaux City, and it is the information 
gathered by Oiran that enables the Thunders to stay 
one step ahead of their rivals and enemies.
Oiran frequently serve as "handlers" for the various 
specialized members of the organization, such as 
its Torakage, Katanaka Snipers, Wastrels, and 
Thunder Archers, ensuring that each member's 
need are met while simultaneously monitoring the 
organization's members for any signs of disloyalty or 
weakness. These meetings frequently take place in 
tea houses, brothels, and the various establishments 
that are somewhere between the two extremes.
When pushed to take matters 
into their own hands, Oiran 
frequently fight with sharpened 
metal claws that have been 
dipped in all manner of 
deadly poisons and toxins.

Text.p906eaced2da2:
Gokudo
The Gokudo are thugs that operate within the 
Little Kingdom district of Malifaux City. While 
they sometimes run protection rackets in that 
neighborhood, they primarily exist to enact the 
wishes of their master, the mysterious Wei Lu.
Membership in the Gokudo is by invitation only, 
and one must be selected by Wei Lu for the honor. 
Once a prospective recruit has undergone the 
necessary training to ensure that she has the skills 
needed to serve her new master, the recruit is finally 
introduced to Wei Lu himself, allowing her to swear 
fealty to the ancient sorcerer.
What the Gokudo don't know is that they are 
actually the descendants of those who swore fealty to 
Wei Lu centuries earlier, and that the oaths of their 
ancestors have been strengthened by the sorcerer's 
magic, making them utterly subservient to his wishes, 
both in this life and the next.

Text.pf976348ed8b4:
Wastrel
Wastrels are people who have been given every 
privilege from birth and have subsequently squandered 
them. They often consider themselves above the law, 
relying upon their family's wealth and good name to 
keep them out of any real trouble. 
Lucas McCabe has gathered a cadre of these ruthless 
men and women around himself to form a (very 
unofficial) group of Guild agents with questionable 
loyalty and ethics. They deal with many of the issues 
that the Guild can't be seen to be officially involved 
in, such as evicting people from Downtown homes 
that are desired by prominent politicians, breaking 
into the homes and offices of M&SU representatives, 
and so on.
What the Guild doesn't realize is that many of these 
Wastrels are also in the pocket of the Ten Thunders, 
most often as a result of their gambling debts finally 
catching up with them. Given the choice between 
serving the Ten Thunders or having their legs 
broken, most Wastrels go with the former option.
The Ten Thunders use Wastrels in much the same 
way as the Guild, calling upon them whenever they 
need a task completed by Westerners who are 
unlikely to seem associated with the Little Kingdom. 
They also spy upon the Guild, using their access to 
the Enclave to intimidate witnesses, make evidence 
disappear, and learn Guild patrol routes. Their 
success rate is somewhat dubious - Wastrels aren't 
trusted by most Guild personnel - but sometimes the 
Ten Thunders don't have many other options.

Text.p2b6346576d8b:
Leopold Von Schill
Tenacious, arrogant, effective. These three words 
sum up the creator and leader of the mercenary band 
known as the Freikorps. On Earth, Von Schill made 
a name for himself as a brave soldier and a cunning 
leader. His uncanny ability to read his opponents 
and place his squad in positions that could best take 
advantage of the flaws in their battle plans earned 
him one promotion after another, as well as more 
medals than he could count.
After retiring from the German military, Von Schill 
was offered a position as a military consultant for 
the Guild, who were preparing their first forays 
through the newly reopened Breach. Von Schill's 
no-nonsense approach to just about everything 
ingratiated him with the Guild's front line troops, 
and though there were few actual conflicts in those 
early days, Von Schill's unit was always prepared for 
the worst.
When Von Schill met with the Governor-General, 
however, the two men proved to be far too alike to 
ever tolerate the other's company. Von Schill rankled 
the Governor-General with his outspoken belief that 
the newly created Quarantine Zones would only lead 
to disaster. Von Schill, in turn, was annoyed by the 
Governor-General's refusal to let military logic take 
precedence over the Guild's desire for Soulstones. 
The meeting ended in shouting voices and a burning 
hatred that lasted all the way up to the GovernorGeneral's untimely death years later.
With his Guild contract terminated, Von Schill 
decided to remain in Malifaux and sell his 
considerable talents to the highest bidder. His time 
working with the Guild had left him with a loyal 
following of soldiers and specialists who weren't 
pleased with the idea of becoming constables and 
police officers. When Von Schill informed them of 
his departure from the Guild, these men and women 
were happy to turn their backs on the Guild in order 
to follow a man they actually respected. With this 
core of loyal, highly skilled soldiers, Von Schill 
created the Freikorps, an elite mercenary group that 
offered its services to anyone that could pay.
Leopold Von Schill

Text.p3c6d3f77aa6a:
Bayou Pig
Unlike the domesticated farm animals back on 
Earth, the pigs of Malifaux are voracious killing 
machines. With skin as thick as leather and massive 
tusks, they're more than capable of knocking an 
adult human to the ground. Once their prey has 
been knocked over, the hungry pig launches into a 
flurry of biting teeth and trampling hooves, tearing 
away flesh with each bite. Even those fortunate 
enough to survive the encounter are often disfigured 
and scarred for life.
Until recent years, the wild pigs of the Bayou kept 
the Gremlin population culled down to a reasonable 
number, and the Gremlins returned the favor by 
hunting the smaller pigs and keeping the pigs in 
check. With the arrival of humanity and gunpowder, 
however, the Gremlins gained the upper hand on 
their porcine neighbors: now, they could hunt even 
the larger pigs, and the pigs they didn't kill, the 
Gremlins forced into captivity. These pigs still aren't 
entirely domesticated - they're a stubborn breed of 
animal - but the Gremlins have made a great deal of 
progress in recent years. 
There's not much going on in the average pig's mind, 
so training a pig to obey orders is mostly a matter 
of constant repetition and frequent jabs from sharp 
sticks. Eventually, the pig realizes that it's easier to 
just eat the food it's given and spend the rest of its 
days sleeping in the mud, which is exactly what the 
Gremlins want.
Of course, there are still plenty of wild pigs roaming 
the swamp, but their numbers just aren't what they 
once were.

Text.p607323d81bf2:
Ansatsu Sniper
When the Ten Thunders wish to eliminate a target 
without getting close, they call on the snipers of the 
Ansatsu dojo. Traditionally, these snipers trained 
with bows, but modern times have shifted their 
focus away from archery and toward rifles, making 
them far deadlier than their ancestors could have 
ever imagined.
All missions given to the Ansatsu snipers are passed 
through the Master of Assassins, the sensei of their 
dojo. The sensei reviews each request asked of the 
Ansatsu, either passing it on to the sniper most 
suited for the task or, more rarely, returning the 
assignment with a refusal to complete it. Such is the 
respect the Ten Thunders have for the Ansatsu that 
these refusals frequently result in the organization 
turning toward more non-lethal means of dealing 
with the troublesome target.
To ensure that they do not reveal the secrets of 
the Katanaka to outsiders, each sniper has his or 
her tongue removed before their first mission. 
The Ansatsu communicate using a gesture-based 
language that is hidden from outsiders - even other 
members of the Ten Thunders - on pain of death.

Text.p3ffb6916f729:
Guild Rifleman
Guild guardsmen who demonstrate exceptional 
marksmanship and discipline are often transferred to 
the Rifleman Corps. There, recruits are put through 
an extensive training regime that teaches them 
improved target selection, battlefield awareness, and 
further marksmanship. Those who finish the training 
are among the most deadly snipers in Malifaux.
Though the Rifleman Corps is often toted as a 
defensive force meant to protect Malifaux City from 
the predations of the Neverborn, the Guild tends 
to use them more as a tool of intimidation. Union 
strikes have a tendency to fall apart when Riflemen 
take up sniping positions on nearby roofs, and a 
few Riflemen stationed on a high ridge will give any 
convict second thoughts about fleeing from their 
work camp.
A select few members of the Rifleman Corps have 
been earmarked by the Elite Division as "distinguished 
agents," which primarily means that they are discrete 
and not likely to raise any objections when told to 
assassinate troublesome (but unarmed) civilians. 
These Riflemen are paid quite well for their silence 
and discretion, but as with most everything the Elite 
Division does, there's a hidden catch. 
The Elite Division can't take its chances with a 
retired soldier exposing its secrets to the world, 
after all, and when one of these "distinguished 
agents" retires, they only have a short time to enjoy 
their wealth before they find themselves caught in 
the sights of a former friend.

Relentless
A life of crime has left this character inured to the 
depravity of the human spirit. Whether forged 
through a childhood spent amidst violence, years 
spent slaving away on a chain gang, or a betrayal 
that left the character with no further illusions 
about angels in the hearts of men, this character has 
become jaded to the terrible things that prowl in the 
shadows of Malifaux.
This character is immune to Horror Duels. 
Duplicitous
Combat isn't always about moving fast. By feinting 
and leading an opponent's attacks, a clever 
combatant can ensure that when her opponent 
finally commits to the attack, it's aimed in entirely 
the wrong direction.
This character may use her Deceive Skill in place 
of her Evade Skill when calculating her Defense 
Derived Aspect. 
Dirty Trick
From the classic maneuver of throwing sand into 
her opponent's eyes to more elaborate tricks, there 
are plenty of ways to throw an opponent off guard. 
What separates the amateur backstabbers from the 
professionals is the ability to follow up that trick 
with a swift attack that takes full advantage of the 
opponent's confusion.
This character gains the following Trigger on the 
Trick Action: 
M Dirty Trick: After succeeding, take a (1) AP 
Close Combat attack against the target, if it is 
in range.
Thugs
This character attracts the service of two Thugs who 
want nothing more than to be her left and right hands 
as the character slowly climbs her way up through 
the ranks of the criminal underworld. These Thugs 
are subordinate characters. 
When this character uses the (1) Order Action to 
command her Thugs, she may command them both, 
and her orders may be different. Alternatively, if this 
character is commanding a single Thug, she may 
treat the (1) Order Action as if it were a (0) Action.
If any of this character's Thugs are killed, she may 
recruit new Thugs at the start of the next session.

Text.pb5b9a331ff8b:
Witchling Stalker
It is dangerous to be a mage when there are Witch 
Hunters such as Sonnia Criid working for the Guild. 
Sonnia excels at killing rogue mages, but those she 
captures are doomed to a worse fate. She turns their 
powers back upon themselves, creating the burned 
and charred creatures known as Witchlings. These 
wretched creatures were once men and women, 
but they have been stripped of their humanity, 
memories, and personalities by the leader of the 
Witch Hunters.
Where Witchlings once channeled powerful 
magical forces, now they can only sense and negate 
the magic of others. This makes them ideal hunting 
dogs for the Witch Hunters, who make liberal use 
of Witchlings not only for their ability to sniff out 
magic but also to send a reminder to others: dabble 
not in strange magics or you might end up as one of 
these terrible creatures.
Some of the fire that Criid uses to burn away a 
Witchling's soul remains within them, smoldering 
like dim coals. During battle, Witchlings can draw 
upon this flame to cloak their blades and bullets in 
magical fire which is further enhanced by the magical 
runes carved into those weapons.
Even the most experienced of mages knows to 
fear the arrival of Witchlings, not only due to their 
powers and what they represent, but also because it 
means that the Witch Hunters have found her scent, 
and they never give up the chase easily.

Text.p3f4a2a0872ab:
Marionette
Though made of wood, these puppets are able to act 
mostly on their own, though they are still bound by 
the strings of their creation, forced to dance whenever 
the puppetmaster holding their strings flicks her 
fingers. Originally crafted by the puppetmaster 
known as Collodi, the secret to creating a Marionette 
- namely, that each one holds the trapped soul of a 
child - has unfortunately spread to others.
Marionettes can walk around of their own volition 
and may choose to attack anyone they see as a threat 
to their owner. Their hands and fingers are made 
of hard wood, and though they lack the strength 
and skill to do any serious damage to a fully grown 
adult, a few Marionettes are more than capable of 
overpowering a child. 
While newly created Marionettes tend to be 
saddened by their new state, often falling into 
depression, time eventually shatters their minds, 
turning all but the most strong-willed of Marionettes 
into cruel predators that can only soothe their pain 
by hurting others. It is a trait that has been harnessed 
time and time again by cruel puppetmasters across 
Malifaux, and now, such shows are watched with 
hesitation and apprehension, instead of joy. 
The authorities in some Contract Towns - 
particularly those who have been visited by Collodi's 
traveling wagon - have taken to outlawing all form of 
puppet shows. Any puppets found by the citizens of 
these troubled towns are dismembered and burnt, 
which has done a great deal to keep the number of 
Marionettes roaming the world down to a minimum.

Text.p89876f182a5b:
Mindless Zombie
Mindless Zombies are among the weakest of all undead. 
They are incapable of higher thought and tend to chase 
just about anything that moves, from late night travelers 
to horse-drawn coaches to shuffling constructs. Though 
individually weak, Mindless Zombies can be dangerous 
in large numbers, as those they kill rise up a short time 
later as new Mindless Zombies.
Left unchecked, a horde of Mindless Zombies can 
become almost unstoppable. Fortunately, the Death 
Marshals take every report of wandering zombies 
seriously, lest an ignored zombie stumble across a 
sleeping family and quickly snowball into a serious 
problem for the Guild.

Text.pc23cc892c7f8: Chained to the floor; the keys are needed to free him.
Text.p2ec7ec540f6b: Start Initiative when the puppets emerge. Remind players about their Pursuits and when their abilities let them draw cards.
Text.p04fc51e265e8: In Scene 2, the Fated may go straight to the engine. Talking to Cesar is optional.
Text.pc8b3790f08f8: Ask each player to introduce their character and describe their appearance. Give them time to talk and get acquainted.
Text.p666c4cda9859: Remind players of their chosen Pursuit for this session. There are no card flips here.
Text.pabbb223b164d: At the end of the Prologue, each participant draws three cards into their Control Hand.
Text.p5f2dd991a923: If nobody helps, the conductor makes Sessa buy another ticket for his trunk, which occupies the seat beside him.
Text.p8f663a767200: Sessa explains that loading convicts bound for the mines delayed the train. Then a whistle sounds, and the train moves toward the silver-blue Breach.
Text.pdb7c030d3d52: A Scream from the Rear Car
Text.pc68edd7e9eea: TN 9 Listen at the rear door reveals electrical crackling. Cesar is killing a guardsman who did not disappear.
Text.pd3ad9d1b3c80: Cesar is unreliable. A separate attempt to read his motives after he offers help reveals that he knows nothing about trains.
Text.pe73acb3a05f0: A truce in exchange for the keys to his shackles.
Text.p63f145d6382a: Make him laugh and win his favor.
Text.p58aede8c135d: Convince him to leave the group alone.
Text.p384e8d099b80: Convince him of a chosen lie.
Text.pe4b0d82dceb6: After every failed Challenge with Cesar, all subsequent TNs with him increase by +1.
Text.p61b3a4a5e05d: Counter: ____ failures. A failed Listen Challenge before the conversation is not a Challenge with Cesar.
Text.pcc3ac5522e87: Success Requirement: 2 × number of Fated. Failure Requirement: 1 × number of Fated.
Text.p00e403bd536a: Interval (5 minutes): ____ · successes: ____ · Margins of Failure: ____
Text.p9188e7be80ea: In either successful-restart outcome, the Fated have reached Malifaux.
Text.pbc6343ed79b7: Use the system's normal buttons for Initiative, ordinary Challenges, weapon attacks, damage and unconsciousness.
Text.p79c1f8ca0242: The Iron Ram will take you through the Breach to Malifaux. For now, you are traveling companions.
Text.pc7fbf2f62e34: A shackled man in a striped convict uniform. Show this when the Fated enter the prison car.
Text.p43fd003b1082: Core Rules, pp. 408–409. A thin, hunched puppetmaster in his late sixties with an enormous trunk marked “Sessa the Amazing.” He disappears with the passengers upon entering the Breach. The book gives him no combat profile: this is a portrait NPC; the default numerical fields are not statistics from the book.
Text.p91ee474884d9: Core Rules, Chapter 11, pp. 411–413. Use the Steamfitter profile (p. 386), without Explosive Demise or My Creation. He is shackled and does not attack first except in self-defense. Failed negotiations increase subsequent TNs by +1. The Fatemaster resolves magical Actions and their suits from the descriptions. His token border is neutral: joining the Arcanists is a possible later outcome.
Text.p63219081117f: Scene 2 prop. Core Rules, p. 412: Cesar killed him with electrical magic, leaving a scorched uniform and a partially melted rifle. This is not a living combatant.
Text.p5df9861a906e: Core Rules, Chapter 11, printed pp. 408–413; PDF page numbers are two higher. The text below is a running adaptation, not a verbatim copy.
Text.p7d7f28c15011: This adventure takes about an hour after character creation. Let players discuss meaningful decisions. Explain the consequences of their choices; do not bend the rules merely to make them win.
Text.p8a8ddc237054: Open scene {ttb:scene:prologue}. The Fated meet in the Iron Ram's third passenger car. No cards are flipped during the Prologue.
Text.p3633f3a2adc4: After introductions, use the normal End Prologue action: each participating Fated draws three cards from their own Twist Deck. Select the actual participants rather than test actors.
Text.pb82c4b8b9bcd: The “Adventure 11 — Place Marionettes” macro creates one hidden opponent per Fated in the battle scene. Enter the number of players; drag their own tokens into the passenger car yourself.
Text.p21d4d0e3c75f: After a successful ending, run the normal Epilogue. In this introductory adventure, the book allows players to adjust their Skills after experiencing the game.
Text.pf37a79be09b9: The map is an original illustrated diagram of three play areas, not an exact blueprint or the train's full length. The engine is on the left, the passenger car in the middle, and the prison car on the right. In the story, other cars remain between the third car and the locomotive; the diagram compresses that journey. One square equals 1 yard. Scenes are not activated automatically. NPCs and notes are visible only to the Fatemaster. Open illustrations in the Player Handouts folder and explicitly show them to players without revealing the Fatemaster's journal.
Text.p90028c20f431: Import adds missing documents while preserving Fatemaster edits and existing tokens. The placement macro does not create another set when Marionettes are already present. The three adventure controls are in the Macros folder.
Text.pc0d20805733b: Core Rules, Chapter 11, printed pp. 408–409; PDF page numbers are two higher. The text below is a running adaptation, not a verbatim copy.
Text.p451bc59ef58e: After hours in the heat outside the Guild station in Breachtown, you are allowed aboard the Iron Ram. Inside, it is surprisingly cold. You sit on facing benches at the front of the third car. Deep scratches above the seats cut into the steel like claw marks.
Text.p22ef6c8841e7: Core Rules, Chapter 11, printed pp. 408–410; PDF page numbers are two higher. The text below is a running adaptation, not a verbatim copy.
Text.p835610b59dd2: As the conductor closes the doors and helps with luggage, a thin elderly passenger across the aisle struggles to lift an enormous trunk. Strain and embarrassment show on his face.
Text.pd6c046b288ac: Helping: TN 8 Athletics. Success stows the trunk overhead. Anyone who tries to help, whether successful or not, notices the words “Sessa the Amazing.”
Text.pb21c666a9c75: Pain and dizziness overwhelm you as the train enters the light. A moment later, the other passengers have vanished. The train is motionless, with no engine noise or clatter of wheels. Silver-blue light pours through the windows. Only scratching from the abandoned trunk breaks the silence.
Text.p41f8a50cb295: Raw magic from the Breach has animated the Marionettes: one per Fated. Strings trail behind them, and they may appear clownish or frightening.
Text.p3325f75bcd9b: If the trunk is on the seat, its lid opens immediately. If overhead, the book allows several shots as it rattles, falls and the puppets emerge. No exact number is given; do not automatically grant a fixed free round.
Text.p951c7f10c426: Start Dramatic Time and Initiative. Marionettes are Minion (5) characters and do not flip cards for ordinary Challenges; their Rank Value is already included in the book's parenthesized totals.
Text.p58fc60a2d9b2: Seats provide Hard Cover: a negative modifier to z attack and damage flips. Climbing across seats counts as Severe terrain and uses twice the movement. The Fatemaster applies these conditional modifiers and movement costs.
Text.p6ea69399263a: Resolve grabbing strings using the Marionette's Trailing Strings Ability. Each has one Fate Point, tracked manually by the Fatemaster.
Text.p281001dbacdb: At 0 Wounds or below, a puppet suffers a Critical Effect and becomes limp and unmoving. After the last Marionette is defeated, end Dramatic Time: players may discard any number of cards and draw back up to three.
Text.p4eac472e7884: Core Rules, Chapter 11, printed pp. 410–412; PDF page numbers are two higher. The text below is a running adaptation, not a verbatim copy.
Text.p71691079cfbc: After the fight, a human scream comes from the next car behind you. At the rear door, a strange muffled crackling can be heard.
Text.p49b76fb1ca8e: Staying achieves nothing; the windows are bolted shut. Going forward leads directly to the engine scene. Investigating the scream leads to the prison car.
Text.pdc539f8602aa: Bright light fills the passage between cars, and something alien moves in the void. Wooden benches line the prison car, with chains rising from the floor. A guardsman's body smolders by the door beside a melted rifle. A man with a heavy square jaw and glowing eyes raises his shackled hands and asks for help.
Text.p488d727e4757: An Irish murderer and thief sentenced by the Guild to mine labor. He gained magic while passing through the Breach; his desire to stop the train holds everyone between worlds. He electrocuted the guardsman but cannot free himself, and the body is beyond his reach. His friendliness is strained, and he has a quick temper. He only attacks first in self-defense.
Text.pca55c422152d: Success at any of these Challenges reveals his surge of power and desire to stop the engine. Freeing him or promising to do so prompts an offer to help restart the train, although he knows nothing about its workings. Use the Steamfitter profile without My Creation and Explosive Demise; resolve magical Actions manually from the profile.
Text.pf9080e8f7c20: Core Rules, Chapter 11, printed p. 413; PDF page numbers are two higher. The text below is a running adaptation, not a verbatim copy.
Text.p6da40ffe154f: Nobody answers in the engine room. The machinery is silent, cold light fills the wide windows, and enormous tentacles move beyond them. The engine looks simple enough: stoke the boiler and operate the controls correctly, and the train should move again.
Text.p1c658def2845: The book lists Athletics, Engineering and Sorcery as allowed Skills and specifies Intellect. Select Intellect in the Challenge dialog for this task.
Text.p9188b353d5d5: Each interval lasts 5 minutes; this is not a time limit for the entire task. Each participant normally makes one Challenge per interval. If the task remains unresolved, another interval begins.
Text.p66822d7074ed: A successful Challenge contributes one success plus one for every Margin of Success (each complete 5 above the TN). An ordinary failure with no Margin of Failure does not change progress. Every Margin of Failure moves the task toward catastrophe. See p. 290.
Text.p3abbe7397ee7: The Fated need not use every allowed Skill. Coal and heat are physical work; controls use Engineering; magical fire uses Sorcery.
Text.p88e2f5b30e62: The explanation mentions Blacksmithing, but the list of allowed Skills does not. The English original contains this discrepancy too. Blacksmithing is not automatically a fourth allowed Skill; allowing it requires an explicit Fatemaster ruling communicated to the group.
Text.pc29dbb2dc33f: The first catastrophe severely damages the engine. One TN 14 Artefacting Challenge can repair it and allow another Restart the Train! Ongoing Challenge. A failed repair or a catastrophe on the second attempt produces the terrible ending. The book gives no alternative routes around this; discuss creative solutions as Fatemaster rulings.
Text.p75552d6b7c4a: The boiler comes to life and the wheels begin to turn. The train accelerates through the light into Malifaux. A Guild engineer jumps aboard the locomotive and brings it to a stop.
Text.peed883cf86a3: If Cesar is free and the group does not turn him in, he pretends to be a fellow passenger, perhaps Vito Sessa if he heard the name. He may later become an ally after joining the Arcanists.
Text.p12b68eb02d3a: If Cesar is turned in or remains shackled, the Guild takes him into custody and, on discovering his powers, turns him into a Witchling Stalker.
Text.p52e88acd1275: The engine ruptures after the failed repairs. Steam shrieks into the space between worlds. A colossal tentacled creature turns toward the noise and approaches the stationary train. The journey is over; nobody will know what happened to the passengers.
Text.p4c71e645542f: Use the normal system Epilogue: Fatemaster-selected Skill advancement, experience and Pursuit steps follow the Epilogue rules. Do not add an arbitrary cash reward; none is specified here. In this introductory session, players may adjust their Skills after learning the system. Record Cesar's fate and the Fated's attitude toward the Guild as hooks for later adventures.
Text.p29942ff1209c: Seats: apply Hard Cover and Severe terrain manually. Geometric walls block movement but do not assign cover.
Text.pd6da5187dcc6: The Fatemaster tracks Marionette Fate Points and strings, Cesar's magical Actions, accumulated successes and Margins of Failure, and the +1 negotiation TN increases.
Text.pcd01a518718e: For NPCs opposing Fated, the Fatemaster currently verifies suits. Do not replace a required suit with a simple numerical TN.
Text.p7d9a8a0372b6: Scenes and illustrations are original visual adaptations. They are not canonical blueprints or character appearances from the book.
Text.p9c1582ba3d85: An elderly passenger with an enormous trunk. Reveal the inscription only after the characters have noticed it.

Text.pb358e1bfcfa0:
Steamfitter
These spellcasters are ostensibly employed by the 
Union in order to keep its various mining constructs 
enchanted and functional. In reality, however, they 
are the core of the Arcanist movement, the men and 
women who believe that the use of magic should be 
free to everyone with the talent for it.
Steamfitters are technically regulated by the Guild, 
but after a decade of fighting with the Union over 
the specifics of that regulation, not to mention the 
greater threat posed by the Arcanists, the Guild has 
more or less left the licensing and regulation of the 
Steamfitters to the Union. Even the Witch Hunters 
are a bit unclear about just what a Steamfitter is 
capable of doing, but thus far, there just hasn't been 
time to investigate them in any great depth.
With access to the hidden vaults of the Arcanists, 
there is almost no bit of magical knowledge that a 
Steamfitter cannot access, given enough time and 
urgency. Most of them are quite adept spellcasters, 
and their profession all but demands that they 
be familiar with constructs and other forms of 
machinery.
